advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make short_root teardown either remove the tree or fail loudly: replace the chmod walk plus `ignore_errors=True` with an rmtree error handler that clears the read-only bit and retries, and re-raises other errors.
evidence: tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py:1-8 docstring: the module asserts that no private-key copy remains in the host temp dir
tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py:33-44 already has a narrower pattern: an rmtree error handler that clears git's read-only bit and retries, and re-raises anything else
advisory.finding: The short_root teardown can leave `tort-*` trees in the system temp dir without any signal. `shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)` swallows every removal failure, and the chmod walk that runs first has no error handling, so if it raises, rmtree never runs. Previously the tree lived under pytest's tmp_path, which pytest's basetemp retention prunes on later runs. Now nothing ever reclaims a partly removed `tort-*` dir. Those dirs hold the nested run's generated ssh keys and any `rebar-opcert-*` key copies, which is the kind of temp-dir leak this test file exists to catch.
scenarios: A file is locked on Windows (e.g. by a lingering git or child process) or a directory is read-only. rmtree gives up silently and the `tort-*` dir, with its key material, stays in %TEMP% permanently.
A chmod or rglob call in the walk raises (e.g. a file disappears mid-walk). Teardown errors out before rmtree, and the whole tree is left behind.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the walk and `ignore_errors=True` with one rmtree call whose error handler clears the read-only bit and retries, re-raising any other error, e.g. `def _retry_writable(func, path, _exc): os.chmod(path, stat.S_IWRITE | stat.S_IREAD); func(path)` and then `shutil.rmtree(root, onerror=_retry_writable)` (`onerror` because requires-python is >=3.11). A failed cleanup then shows up as a teardown error instead of a silent leak.

coaching.coaching: File a follow-on ticket (discovered_from this change) for the silent cleanup failure handling in short_root teardown, a pre-existing / out-of-scope issue — do not fix it in this change.
coaching.subject: the silent cleanup failure handling in short_root teardown
